<reflection>
The third experiment (low substrate, 0.2 M) succeeded in shifting the negative log-likelihood values but did not break the degeneracy among the top four mechanisms (M7, M3, M6, M8). These models remain closely matched, indicating that varying substrate and catalyst concentrations alone may not be sufficient to discriminate them. My aim for the third turn—to probe saturation effects—was partially achieved, but further orthogonal information is needed. Introducing product into the initial mixture is a logical next step, as it can reveal reversibility, product inhibition, and differential inactivation pathways that are not apparent in product-free experiments.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
I propose an experiment with initial product concentration of 0.1 M, substrate at 0.5 M, and catalyst at 0.01 M. This design introduces a new dimension by including product, which will test reversible steps and product-dependent inactivation. Mechanisms with explicit product inhibition (e.g., M12, M17) may show stronger deceleration, while reversible mechanisms (all top candidates have reversible steps) may exhibit altered net rates due to reverse reaction. Importantly, mechanisms involving product-induced inactivation (M12, M17) or product binding (M4, M8 with ligand?) could display distinct time profiles. The moderate substrate concentration ensures that forward progress is still observable, avoiding extreme conditions that might mask differences. This experiment is informative across many candidates simultaneously, as it probes a regime not yet explored in the previous runs.
</hypothesis>
